CHIEF COMPLAINT
Anxiety management follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports that her anxiety has improved on Buspar, which was recently started by Dr. Brown. She describes severe anxiety in November and December that began during the day at work. She notes that the week before her period, her anxiety would spike significantly, and then it progressed to random anxiety spikes without apparent reason. She was started on Singulair by Dr. Ward during that time period and wonders if that medication contributed to her anxiety, as Singulair can cause anxiety. She attributes some of the stress to work-related factors, including leading the process of delivering COVID results to patients at the beginning of the pandemic, which required her to open evaluation centers and a COVID clinic. She also experienced feelings of guilt and selfish feelings about having anxiety while not being on the front lines like physicians and nurses. She notes the stressful "golive" in November and December. She stopped taking Camila birth control because it was causing increased hunger. She has lost some weight over the past six months. The doctor discussed the possibility of hormonal factors contributing to her anxiety, noting she was on progesterone for period regulation. Patient reports currently feeling much better.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies weight loss (though reports losing weight over past six months after stopping Camila). She reports breast tenderness and palpable lumps in the left breast, which she describes as smaller than before but still present. She had previous clogging and soreness when breastfeeding. She reports itching or discomfort in the genital area, which she manages with cream used once weekly with good effect. She requests refill of the cream.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Abnormal Pap smear around 2009, requiring follow-up every six months, which subsequently normalized. History of breast lumps and fibroadenomas. Last Pap smear in 2019 was negative/negative.

MEDICATIONS
Buspar, progesterone, Singulair (recently started), cream for genital itching/discomfort.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at approximately age 45.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in a healthcare setting related to COVID testing and patient result delivery. She is married with two children (daughter and son). Husband has not received COVID vaccine. Daughter shares father's vaccine concerns. Son has received first COVID vaccine dose. Patient has received COVID vaccine.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Neck: Small bumps palpated, patient notes they are smaller than previously. Breasts: Left breast slightly denser with tenderness noted. Palpable lumps present but patient reports they feel smaller. Genitalia: Appears normal.

RESULTS
Pap smear from 2019 was negative/negative.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety: Improved on Buspar. Discussed possible hormonal component. Continue current management.
2. Breast lumps/fibroadenomas: Continue monitoring. Palpable lumps present but stable. Referral placed to breast specialist for further evaluation and surveillance, including possible in-office ultrasound. Patient will be contacted within couple of business days to schedule appointment.
3. Cervical cancer screening: Repeat Pap smear ordered given history of abnormal Pap in 2009 and increased risk factors noted by provider.
4. Genital itching/discomfort: Cream refill requested.
